path="/mnt/data/713f7b5df54882d9d505baa2b242c462-data.json"

import os, json, math, sys, platform, textwrap
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager, ft2font
from matplotlib.transforms import Bbox

# ---------- Read and independently compute ----------
src = "/mnt/data/713f7b5df54882d9d505baa2b242c462-data.json"
with open(src, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    d = json.load(f)

assert d["figure_kind"] == "violin"
obs = d["observations"]
values = np.asarray([r["y"] for r in obs if r.get("y") is not None], dtype=np.float64)
if values.size < 3:
    raise ValueError("Each violin group requires at least three valid records.")
s2 = float(np.var(values, ddof=1))
if not (s2 > 0 and math.isfinite(s2)):
    raise ValueError("Each violin group requires positive sample variance.")

n = int(values.size)
factor = n ** (-1.0/5.0)
bandwidth = math.sqrt(s2) * factor
grid = np.linspace(float(values.min()), float(values.max()), 256, dtype=np.float64)
kde = gaussian_kde(values, bw_method="scott")
density = np.asarray(kde(grid), dtype=np.float64)
q1, median, q3 = [float(x) for x in np.quantile(values, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], method="linear")]

series = [{
    "group": None,
    "n": n,
    "bandwidth": float(bandwidth),
    "min": float(values.min()),
    "max": float(values.max()),
    "grid": [float(x) for x in grid],
    "density": [float(x) for x in density],
    "q1": q1,
    "median": median,
    "q3": q3
}]

# ---------- Font coverage ----------
def collect_strings(x):
    out = []
    if isinstance(x, str):
        out.append(x)
    elif isinstance(x, dict):
        for v in x.values():
            out.extend(collect_strings(v))
    elif isinstance(x, list):
        for v in x:
            out.extend(collect_strings(v))
    return out

all_text = "".join(collect_strings({
    "labels": d["labels"],
    "presentation": d["presentation"]
}))
needed = {ord(ch) for ch in all_text if ch not in "\n\r\t"}
font_candidates = [
    "Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans CJK JP", "Source Han Sans SC",
    "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "Arial Unicode MS", "DejaVu Sans"
]
font_path = None
font_name = None
for candidate in font_candidates:
    try:
        p = font_manager.findfont(candidate, fallback_to_default=False)
        cmap = ft2font.FT2Font(p).get_charmap()
        if needed.issubset(cmap.keys()):
            font_path = p
            font_name = font_manager.FontProperties(fname=p).get_name()
            break
    except Exception:
        pass
if font_path is None:
    # Exhaustive installed-font inspection
    for p in font_manager.findSystemFonts(fontext="ttf") + font_manager.findSystemFonts(fontext="otf"):
        try:
            cmap = ft2font.FT2Font(p).get_charmap()
            if needed.issubset(cmap.keys()):
                font_path = p
                font_name = font_manager.FontProperties(fname=p).get_name()
                break
        except Exception:
            continue
if font_path is None:
    raise RuntimeError("No installed font covers all supplied glyphs.")
fp = font_manager.FontProperties(fname=font_path)

# ---------- Exact output JSON ----------
result = {
    "schema_version": 5,
    "figure_kind": d["figure_kind"],
    "language": d["language"],
    "plot_config": d["plot_config"],
    "title": d["labels"]["title"],
    "x_label": d["labels"]["x_label"],
    "y_label": d["labels"]["y_label"],
    "caption": d["labels"]["caption"],
    "statistics": {"series": series},
    "presentation": d["presentation"],
    "environment": {
        "python_version": platform.python_version(),
        "matplotlib_version": matplotlib.__version__,
        "font": font_name
    }
}
result_path = "/mnt/data/result.json"
with open(result_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(result, f, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, separators=(",", ":"))

# ---------- Figure ----------
W = int(d["plot_config"]["style"]["width"])
H = int(d["plot_config"]["style"]["height"])
DPI = 300
FS = float(d["plot_config"]["style"]["font_size"])
assert W > 0 and H > 0
matplotlib.rcParams.update({
    "font.size": FS,
    "font.family": font_name,
    "text.usetex": False,
    "mathtext.default": "regular",
    "axes.unicode_minus": True,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "savefig.facecolor": "white",
})

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W / DPI, H / DPI), dpi=DPI, facecolor="white")

# Helpers for width-aware wrapping, preserving all non-whitespace characters/words.
fig.canvas.draw()
renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()

def text_width_px(s, fontsize=FS, weight="normal"):
    t = fig.text(-10, -10, s, fontsize=fontsize, fontproperties=fp,
                 fontweight=weight, parse_math=False)
    fig.canvas.draw()
    w = t.get_window_extent(renderer=fig.canvas.get_renderer()).width
    t.remove()
    return w

def wrap_to_px(text, max_px, fontsize=FS):
    words = text.split(" ")
    lines, cur = [], ""
    for word in words:
        trial = word if not cur else cur + " " + word
        if cur and text_width_px(trial, fontsize) > max_px:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = word
        else:
            cur = trial
    if cur:
        lines.append(cur)
    return "\n".join(lines)

left = 0.105
right = 0.965
text_left = 0.055
text_right = 0.965
max_text_px = (text_right - text_left) * W

caption = d["labels"]["caption"]
abbr = "; ".join(f'{a["term"]}: {a["definition"]}' for a in d["presentation"]["abbreviations"])
caption_wrapped = wrap_to_px(caption, max_text_px, FS)
abbr_wrapped = wrap_to_px(abbr, max_text_px, FS)

# Add explanatory text first, measure it, then allocate the data axes above it.
abbr_text = fig.text(text_left, 0.035, abbr_wrapped, ha="left", va="bottom",
                     fontsize=FS, fontproperties=fp, color="#222222",
                     linespacing=1.18, parse_math=False)
fig.canvas.draw()
abbr_bbox = abbr_text.get_window_extent(renderer=fig.canvas.get_renderer())
abbr_top = abbr_bbox.y1 / H

caption_bottom = abbr_top + 0.025
caption_text = fig.text(text_left, caption_bottom, caption_wrapped, ha="left", va="bottom",
                        fontsize=FS, fontproperties=fp, color="#222222",
                        linespacing=1.18, parse_math=False)
fig.canvas.draw()
caption_bbox = caption_text.get_window_extent(renderer=fig.canvas.get_renderer())
caption_top = caption_bbox.y1 / H

# Dedicated title region.
title_text = fig.text(0.5, 0.965, d["labels"]["title"], ha="center", va="top",
                      fontsize=FS, fontproperties=fp, fontweight="bold",
                      color="#111111", parse_math=False)
fig.canvas.draw()
title_bbox = title_text.get_window_extent(renderer=fig.canvas.get_renderer())
title_bottom = title_bbox.y0 / H

# Maintain a clear gap between axes/ticks and caption.
axes_bottom = caption_top + 0.075
axes_top = title_bottom - 0.040
if axes_top - axes_bottom < 0.20:
    raise RuntimeError("Insufficient canvas for non-overlapping required regions.")
ax = fig.add_axes([left, axes_bottom, right-left, axes_top-axes_bottom])

# Colorblind palette, first categorical color.
body_color = "#0173B2"
edge_color = "#014B78"
max_d = float(np.max(density))
half_width = 0.36 * density / max_d
ax.fill_betweenx(grid, -half_width, half_width, facecolor=body_color,
                 edgecolor=edge_color, linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.88)
# Quartile overlays.
for qv in (q1, q3):
    hw = float(np.interp(qv, grid, half_width))
    ax.plot([-0.55*hw, 0.55*hw], [qv, qv], color="white", linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=3)
hwm = float(np.interp(median, grid, half_width))
ax.plot([-0.72*hwm, 0.72*hwm], [median, median], color="#111111",
        linewidth=2.2, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=4)

ax.set_xlim(-0.55, 0.55)
yr = float(values.max() - values.min())
ax.set_ylim(float(values.min()) - 0.04*yr, float(values.max()) + 0.04*yr)
ax.set_xticks([0.0])
ax.set_xticklabels([""], fontproperties=fp, fontsize=FS)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)
for lab in ax.get_yticklabels():
    lab.set_fontproperties(fp)
    lab.set_fontsize(FS)

# Presentation axes labels and units exactly, without adding text when unit is empty.
px = d["presentation"]["axes"]["x"]
py = d["presentation"]["axes"]["y"]
x_axis_text = px["label"] if px["unit"] == "" else f'{px["label"]} ({px["unit"]})'
y_axis_text = py["label"] if py["unit"] == "" else f'{py["label"]} ({py["unit"]})'
ax.set_xlabel(x_axis_text, fontsize=FS, fontproperties=fp, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel(y_axis_text, fontsize=FS, fontproperties=fp, labelpad=10)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#D9D9D9", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.8)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#555555")
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#555555")

# Final renderer inspection: text inside canvas and mutually separated.
fig.canvas.draw()
renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
canvas = Bbox.from_bounds(0, 0, W, H)
text_boxes = {
    "title": title_text.get_window_extent(renderer),
    "caption": caption_text.get_window_extent(renderer),
    "abbreviations": abbr_text.get_window_extent(renderer),
    "x_label": ax.xaxis.label.get_window_extent(renderer),
    "y_label": ax.yaxis.label.get_window_extent(renderer),
}
# Include nonempty tick labels.
for i, lab in enumerate(ax.get_yticklabels()):
    if lab.get_text():
        text_boxes[f"ytick_{i}"] = lab.get_window_extent(renderer)
for i, lab in enumerate(ax.get_xticklabels()):
    if lab.get_text():
        text_boxes[f"xtick_{i}"] = lab.get_window_extent(renderer)

for name, bb in text_boxes.items():
    if bb.x0 < -1 or bb.y0 < -1 or bb.x1 > W+1 or bb.y1 > H+1:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Text clipping detected: {name} {bb.bounds}")

# Required major-region separation.
if text_boxes["caption"].overlaps(text_boxes["abbreviations"]):
    raise RuntimeError("Caption overlaps abbreviations.")
if text_boxes["title"].overlaps(ax.get_window_extent(renderer)):
    raise RuntimeError("Title overlaps data axes.")
if text_boxes["caption"].overlaps(ax.get_window_extent(renderer)):
    raise RuntimeError("Caption overlaps data axes.")
if text_boxes["caption"].overlaps(text_boxes["x_label"]) and x_axis_text:
    raise RuntimeError("Caption overlaps x-axis label.")

figure_path = "/mnt/data/figure.png"
fig.savefig(figure_path, dpi=DPI, facecolor="white", edgecolor="none",
            bbox_inches=None, pad_inches=0)
plt.close(fig)

# Verify exact raster dimensions and files.
from PIL import Image
with Image.open(figure_path) as im:
    dims = im.size
    mode = im.mode
assert dims == (W, H), (dims, (W, H))
os.path.getsize(result_path), os.path.getsize(figure_path), dims, mode, font_name, bandwidth
# Re-open result and verify allowed top-level keys and finite numeric values.
with open("/mnt/data/result.json","r",encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rr=json.load(f)
allowed={"schema_version","figure_kind","language","plot_config","title","x_label","y_label","caption","statistics","presentation","environment"}
assert set(rr)==allowed
def verify_finite(x):
    if isinstance(x, float):
        assert math.isfinite(x)
    elif isinstance(x, dict):
        for v in x.values(): verify_finite(v)
    elif isinstance(x, list):
        for v in x: verify_finite(v)
verify_finite(rr)
# Confirm presentation is an exact deep copy and labels flattened exactly.
assert rr["presentation"] == data["presentation"]
assert rr["title"] == data["labels"]["title"]
assert rr["x_label"] == data["labels"]["x_label"]
assert rr["y_label"] == data["labels"]["y_label"]
assert rr["caption"] == data["labels"]["caption"]
print("verified", len(rr["statistics"]["series"][0]["grid"]), len(rr["statistics"]["series"][0]["density"]))
